A Brazilian novelist, poet and story writer, widely seen as the greatest writer in Brazilian literature. He was born in Rio de Janeiro, the grandson of freed slaves, to a poor family, and had little formal schooling.

He started as a typesetter and proofreader, wrote for newspapers, and later became a senior civil servant, all while writing. His early novels were romantic. Then, with The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas (1881), told by a dead man, he turned to a sharp, ironic and playful style, decades ahead of his time. His best known works:

  • The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas (1881)
  • Quincas Borba (1891)
  • Dom Casmurro (1899), whose jealous narrator leaves readers unsure if his wife was unfaithful

His books show the Rio of the empire of Pedro II and its elite, slavery and vanity, without preaching. In 1897 he founded the Brazilian Academy of Letters and was its first president. He lived to see slavery abolished in 1888.
